description: Reviewed cardiacCore allowlist for the approximate C++ dictionary-key scanner (omnidriver.openfoam.dict_keys_scanner), the same mechanism and format as omnidriver-cardiacfoam's. Written 2026-09-28 from the first scan of cardiacCore main (f0fc231) src/. It found one real catalog gap, setCardiacAnatomy.C's rvLocalBands (getOrDefault<label>, default 10), now catalogued; the rest are waived here, in three groups. (a) NOT A DICTIONARY KEY: 'name' (1DgraphToFoam.C), 'maxEdgeLength' and 'internalRole' (refine1Dgraph.C) are argList command-line options (args.getOrDefault), not dictionary reads. (b) NOT A CATALOGUED INPUT DICTIONARY: 'points', 'conductionEdges', 'pvjNodes', 'pvjResistances' are read by foamTo1Dgraph.C from a Purkinje graph file (constant/purkinjeGraph), a generated file no study writes; 1DgraphToFoam.C writes the same names. (c) SCAR IS OFF MAIN: every $CARDIAC_SCAR and $PURKINJE_SCAR path, and the scar sub-dictionaries 'channels' and 'purkinjeScarPolicy', are catalogued from the scar branch (catalogs/inputs.py, 'scar-branch:' source_refs); main deleted src/setCardiacScar and src/setPurkinjeScar in c53a0d7, so no C++ on main reads them. Scanning the scar branch instead would make (c) unused and fail, as it should. 'regions' is the scar catalogue's $PURKINJE_SCAR.regions.<region_id> container, same reason.
